hook: A'ja Wilson Just Made WNBA History With *5* MVPs
dek: She's now tied with Bill Russell and Michael Jordan for the most MVPs ever.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: A'ja Wilson was named the *2026 WNBA MVP*, her 5th award and 3rd straight.

slides.label: The numbers
slides.text: This is her *4th MVP in five seasons*, making her the first player in WNBA history to win 5.

slides.label: Rare company
slides.text: She now joins *Bill Russell* and *Michael Jordan* as the only players with 5 MVPs across the NBA and WNBA.

slides.label: Still chasing
slides.text: Only *Kareem Abdul-Jabbar* has more, he holds the record with 6 MVPs.

slides.label: More hardware
slides.text: This year she also won 2 *ESPY Awards* and a *BET Award* for Sportswoman of the Year.

slides.label: On the court
slides.text: She's averaging *26.2 points* a game, leading the reigning champion *Las Vegas Aces* to the semifinals.

slides.label: What's next
slides.text: Game 3 against the *Golden State Valkyries* is tonight, with a title and a 6th MVP both on the line.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: Her dominance comes right after a historic *CBA* win, backing up the case for real investment in women's sports and the athletes who built it.

question: Will she catch Kareem's 6 MVPs? Yes or no.

caption_instagram:
A'ja Wilson just became the first player in WNBA history to win 5 MVP awards, and she did it three years in a row. The Las Vegas Aces star picked up the 2026 WNBA MVP, her 4th in five seasons, putting her in rare company with Bill Russell and Michael Jordan as the only players across the NBA and WNBA with 5 MVPs. Only Kareem Abdul-Jabbar has more, with 6.

This year alone she also took home 2 ESPY Awards and a BET Award for Sportswoman of the Year. On the court, she's averaging 26.2 points per game and has the defending champion Aces back in the semifinals, with Game 3 against the Golden State Valkyries tonight.

Her MVP run lands right after WNBA players secured a historic CBA, adding real proof to the case for investing in women's sports. (via EBONY)
